title: Rendering section applies CSS properties to form controls where behavior is (currently) undefined
body:
Issue
-----

The spec should explain the current inconsistent situation where rendering of most form controls is undefined (or not well-defined), but there can still be style rules for these elements in the spec, because some things do have a consistent effect in browsers and we can improve interop for the UA stylesheet somewhat independently of defining how form controls are actually rendered.

Context
-----

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#form-controls

> input, select, option, optgroup, button, textarea \{
>   text\-indent:​ initial;
> \}

Gecko has a `text-indent` declaration for `option` and `optgroup`, while WebKit and Chromium do not.

https://dxr.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/c909c105f914f69054b9a7c6b189ee39fa1cad44/layout/style/res/forms.css#354
https://dxr.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/c909c105f914f69054b9a7c6b189ee39fa1cad44/layout/style/res/forms.css#388

https://github.com/WebKit/webkit/blob/89c28d471fae35f1788a0f857067896a10af8974/Source/WebCore/css/html.css#L360 (does not include `option`/`optgroup`)

https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/1d11dcde0f28df41b6e7c454257452289ae03a51/third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/resources/html.css#406  (does not include `option`/`optgroup`)

In any case, the effect of `text-indent` on `option` is undefined, since it's in a `select` which is a form control which is effectively a replaced element (at least for some `-webkit-appearance` values, but this is also still being figured out). Should the spec include rules where the effect is undefined?

In some cases, I think the answer is yes. In particular, for https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1310 there was a case of a difference in UA stylesheets that affected rendering in browsers and this was wasting web developers' time.

In the case mentioned in this issue (`text-indent` on `option`/`optgroup`, it's unclear whether it's an important interoperability issue. This would probably need some investigation.
